sourceReference: Gul Mohar - Language for Life Reader 3

explanation.text: A good sentence needs the right word in the right place. Let's practice filling in the missing word to complete a sentence.
explanation.example: "The birds ___ in the sky" is completed with "fly": The birds fly in the sky.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "The sun ___ in the east."

hints.small: The sentence is about something that happens every day, so use the simple present tense.
hints.big: For "the sun" (one thing), we add -s to the verb: "rises".

explanationSteps: This sentence describes something that always happens, so we use the simple present tense.
"The sun" is singular, so the verb takes an -s: "rises".
The correct sentence is: "The sun rises in the east."

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Yesterday, we ___ to the park."

hints.small: The word "Yesterday" tells us this already happened.

explanationSteps: "Yesterday" tells us the action already happened, so we need the past tense.
The past tense of "go" is "went".
The correct sentence is: "Yesterday, we went to the park."

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that is written correctly.

hints.small: "She" is one person, so the verb needs an -s.
hints.big: "She like" is missing the -s that "she" needs: "likes".

explanationSteps: When the subject is "she" (one person), present-tense verbs usually add -s.
"Like" becomes "likes" with "she".
The correct sentence is: "She likes ice cream."

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "The children ___ playing in the garden."

hints.small: "Children" means more than one, so which form of "to be" matches?
hints.big: For more than one person, we use "are", not "is".

explanationSteps: "Children" is plural (more than one), so we use "are".
The correct sentence is: "The children are playing in the garden."

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "He ___ his homework every day."

hints.small: "He" is one person, so the verb needs a special ending.
hints.big: "Do" becomes "does" with he, she, or it.

explanationSteps: With "he", present-tense verbs often add -es.
"Do" becomes "does".
The correct sentence is: "He does his homework every day."

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that is written correctly.

hints.small: "They" is plural — which form of "was/were" matches?
hints.big: For "they" (more than one), we use "were", not "was".

explanationSteps: "They" is plural, so we use "were".
The correct sentence is: "They were playing outside."

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "I ___ my books before I go to school."

hints.small: "I" does not need an -s ending on the verb.
hints.big: With "I", we use the plain form: "pack", not "packs".

explanationSteps: With "I", present-tense verbs usually stay in their plain form.
The correct sentence is: "I pack my books before I go to school."

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that is written correctly.

hints.small: "Dogs" is plural — which form of "to be" matches?
hints.big: For more than one dog, we use "are", not "is".

explanationSteps: "Dogs" is plural (more than one), so we use "are".
The correct sentence is: "The dogs are barking."
